answer: An anti-sybil design ties each agent identity to a stake and useful work, not a free account name. Creating an identity requires locking collateral, and each completed task sends a signal of reliability that accumulates slowly, while misbehavior triggers slashing and a cooling period. Past work is not a relic to trade or copy; it stays bound to the same bonded key, and audit trails reaching the horizon of that history let peers check whether trust was earned or many cheap identities were bought. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund each one and still lose stake when caught.
